notes: In 4.3, dependency-scan-pipeline-execution replaces dependency-scan-repository-aggregation because the page's rule for closing an alert detected by several pipelines is ambiguous; the card tests the documented pipeline-based execution instead. In 5.2, kql-take-arbitrary-rows replaces vm-cpu-metric-guest-scope because the host versus guest metric split is the other side of 5.1's vm-guest-azure-monitor-agent; application-sampled-search-view replaces application-percentile-outliers because the current Application Insights investigation page documents a duration distribution rather than percentile outlier analysis, and a KQL percentile card would tilt 5.2 further toward KQL. In review: storage-server-e2e-latency-distinction became storage-transactions-response-type in 5.2 because the E2E versus Server latency answer could be read from the metric names.

cards.statement: GitHub Advanced Security for Azure DevOps can scan Team Foundation Version Control repositories in Azure Repos.
cards.explanation: GitHub Advanced Security for Azure DevOps covers Azure Repos Git repositories on Azure DevOps Services; TFVC repositories fall outside its scope.
cards.misconception: Advanced Security covers every repository type that Azure Repos hosts.
tags: GitHub Advanced Security for Azure DevOps
cards.volatilityNote: Microsoft could extend the repository types or hosting options that Advanced Security supports.

source.title: Configure GitHub Advanced Security for Azure DevOps features

cards.statement: In Azure Repos, GitHub Advanced Security push protection evaluates only pushes made after it is enabled.
cards.explanation: Secrets committed earlier, including those in historical commits, surface through repository secret scanning, which starts in the background when the feature is turned on.
tags: GitHub Advanced Security for Azure DevOps

source.title: Configure GitHub Advanced Security for Azure DevOps features

cards.statement: GitHub Code Security for Azure DevOps starts dependency scanning once an engineer enables it on a repository.
cards.explanation: Dependency scanning is pipeline-based: it runs in a pipeline with the dependency scanning task or in a repository with dependency scanning default setup, not on enablement alone.
cards.misconception: Enabling the product scans a repository's dependencies by itself.
tags: GitHub Code Security for Azure DevOps

source.title: Set up dependency scanning for GitHub Advanced Security

cards.statement: Microsoft recommends starting Azure Repos code scanning with CodeQL default setup rather than advanced setup.
cards.explanation: Default setup runs CodeQL on a schedule through Azure Pipelines and configures the detected languages itself; teams that need custom build steps, other agent pools or more branches add advanced setup.
tags: GitHub Advanced Security for Azure DevOps

source.title: Configure GitHub Advanced Security for Azure DevOps features

cards.statement: Enabling GitHub Advanced Security on an Azure DevOps project's existing repositories also covers later ones.
cards.explanation: Project-level enablement applies to existing repositories; the separate Automatically enable Advanced Security for new repositories setting covers repositories created afterward.
cards.misconception: Bulk enablement automatically extends to future repositories.
tags: GitHub Advanced Security for Azure DevOps

source.title: Configure GitHub Advanced Security for Azure DevOps features

cards.statement: Microsoft Defender for Cloud lists onboarded Azure DevOps, GitHub and GitLab resources in one DevOps inventory.
cards.explanation: DevOps security in Defender for Cloud gives security teams a central view of connected environments, with code, secret, dependency and IaC findings per resource.

source.title: Microsoft Defender for Cloud DevOps security

cards.statement: Defender for Cloud needs engineers to map GitHub repositories to workloads before GHAS findings get runtime context.
cards.explanation: Through the GitHub connector, Defender for Cloud maps repositories to running workloads automatically and raises GHAS findings with risk factors such as internet exposure.
cards.misconception: Code-to-runtime mapping is a manual setup step.
cards.volatilityNote: The GitHub Advanced Security integration with Defender for Cloud is recent and its capabilities can evolve.

source.title: GitHub Advanced Security integration with Microsoft Defender for Cloud

cards.statement: Dependabot can open an alert on an unchanged repository when GitHub adds a matching advisory to its database.
cards.explanation: Dependabot scans the default branch and alerts both when the dependency graph changes and when a new vulnerability enters the GitHub Advisory Database.

cards.statement: Microsoft Defender for Cloud waits until a container image runs in a cluster before assessing its vulnerabilities.
cards.explanation: Registry vulnerability assessment scans images in supported registries such as Azure Container Registry before deployment; runtime assessment adds coverage for running containers.
cards.misconception: Container vulnerability assessment starts at runtime.

cards.statement: CodeQL run outside the container that compiles the code can fail with No source code was seen during the build.
cards.explanation: CodeQL has to monitor a compiled language's build, so GitHub says to run it inside the container in which the code is built, both with the CodeQL CLI and with GitHub Actions.

source.title: Running CodeQL code scanning in a container

cards.statement: Microsoft recommends the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Distro for most code-based server-side Application Insights setups.
cards.explanation: Server-side web apps, VMs and AKS workloads follow one path: create the Application Insights resource, add the Distro and configure the connection string.

cards.statement: The instrumentation key in an Application Insights connection string authenticates the app's telemetry ingestion.
cards.explanation: The instrumentation key identifies the target resource and is not a security token or key; authenticated ingestion uses Microsoft Entra ID.
cards.misconception: The instrumentation key acts as a secret credential for ingestion.

cards.statement: Azure Monitor Storage insights shows a storage account's capacity once an engineer adds a diagnostic setting.
cards.explanation: Storage insights needs nothing enabled or configured; it uses the storage metrics that Azure collects by default from each storage account.
cards.misconception: Storage insights depends on diagnostic settings to collect its data.

source.title: Monitor Azure Storage services with Azure Monitor Storage insights

cards.statement: Azure Monitor Network Insights saves an engineer's edits as a new workbook in a chosen resource group.
cards.explanation: Edit mode changes the workbook view, and saving stores the result as a new workbook tied to a designated subscription and resource group.

cards.statement: Azure Monitor managed service for Prometheus can collect AKS container stdout and stderr logs.
cards.explanation: Container log collection uses a containerized Azure Monitor agent to send stdout, stderr and Kubernetes events to Log Analytics; managed Prometheus collects metrics.
cards.misconception: Managed Prometheus collects container logs as well as metrics.

cards.statement: Enabling enhanced monitoring on an Azure VM installs Azure Monitor agent to collect guest data.
cards.explanation: Azure collects host metrics automatically; enhanced monitoring installs Azure Monitor agent on the VM and starts collecting a default set of guest metrics.
cards.volatilityNote: The VM monitoring experience recently added OpenTelemetry guest metrics and can change further.

cards.statement: GitHub insights for Projects keeps archived items in a project's historical charts.
cards.explanation: Insights charts use the items in a project as source data and stop tracking items that are archived or deleted.
cards.misconception: Archiving an item preserves it in project insights.

cards.statement: Azure DevOps subscriptions to completed build events offer a filter on the pipeline's definition name.
cards.explanation: The Build completed event exposes fields such as Definition name, Status and Build reason, so a team can be alerted about specific pipelines and outcomes.

cards.statement: An Application Insights standard test checks the SSL certificate of each URL in a redirect chain.
cards.explanation: A standard test follows redirects but validates the SSL certificate on the final redirected URL alone.
cards.misconception: Certificate validation covers every hop of a redirect chain.

cards.statement: A GitHub user can limit GitHub Actions notifications from watched repositories to failed workflow runs.
cards.explanation: The Actions notification setting Only notify for failed workflows delivers workflow run updates when a run fails.

cards.statement: In KQL, requests | where duration > 1000 drops rows whose duration value is null.
cards.explanation: KQL filter comparisons return false for null values, so those rows fail the predicate; functions such as isnull() handle them explicitly.

cards.statement: In KQL, requests | project name, duration returns those two columns followed by the table's other columns.
cards.explanation: project keeps the columns named in its arguments, in that order, and drops every other input column.
cards.misconception: project reorders columns while keeping the rest.

cards.statement: In KQL, requests | summarize count() by timestamp groups the table's rows into hourly bins automatically.
cards.explanation: Automatic hourly bins for datetime columns are no longer supported; summarize count() by bin(timestamp, 1h) groups the rows by hour.
cards.misconception: summarize bins datetime group keys by itself.

cards.statement: In KQL, several ago() calls in one query statement use the same current UTC time.
cards.explanation: Like now(), ago() references one UTC clock value per query statement, so ago(1h) and ago(1d) measure back from the same instant.

cards.statement: In KQL, requests | take 10 returns the ten most recent requests in the table.
cards.explanation: take returns up to the given number of rows with no guarantee which ones unless the data is sorted, and repeated runs can differ.

cards.statement: Application Insights transaction diagnostics shows the telemetry sharing one Operation ID in a single view.
cards.explanation: The end-to-end transaction details view correlates requests, dependencies and exceptions from monitored components through their shared operation.

source.title: Investigate failures, performance, and transactions with Application Insights

cards.statement: With external calls fully instrumented, leftover Application Insights Gantt chart time is likely in-process work.
cards.explanation: Gantt chart time that no tracked dependency covers comes from uninstrumented external calls or in-process work; with all calls instrumented, the .NET Profiler helps diagnose the process.

source.title: Investigate failures, performance, and transactions with Application Insights

cards.statement: Application Insights live metrics stores its streamed data for later queries in Log Analytics.
cards.explanation: Live metrics data persists while it is on the chart and is then discarded; metrics explorer and Log Analytics hold the retained telemetry.
cards.misconception: Live metrics doubles as a retained data store.

source.title: Live metrics: real-time monitoring in Application Insights

cards.statement: With sampling on, Application Insights Search lists each telemetry item that the application emitted.
cards.explanation: With sampling enabled, the Failures, Performance, Search and transaction views show the telemetry retained after sampling rather than every emitted item.
cards.misconception: Portal investigation views show unsampled telemetry.

source.title: Investigate failures, performance, and transactions with Application Insights

cards.statement: The Azure Storage Transactions metric counts failed requests together with successful ones in one total.
cards.explanation: Transactions includes successful requests, failed requests and requests that produced errors; splitting it by the ResponseType dimension separates the kinds of response.

source.title: Azure Blob Storage monitoring data reference
